question: Complete: ___ ag foghlaim Gaeilge.
explanation: Tá mé ag foghlaim Gaeilge means “I am learning Irish.” The progressive construction uses tá + ag + verbal noun.

question: Complete: Is ___ mé. (I am a teacher.)
explanation: Is múinteoir mé is a standard way to say “I am a teacher.”

question: How do you say “I have a book”?
explanation: Irish expresses possession with tá + thing + ag + person: Tá leabhar agam.

question: Complete: Tá an cat ___ an chathaoir. (The cat is on the chair.)
explanation: Ar means “on”. Ar an gcathaoir means “on the chair”.

question: Which is a common Irish greeting?
explanation: Dia duit is a common way to say “hello”. Oíche mhaith means “good night”, and slán means “goodbye”.

question: Complete: Chuaigh mé ___ an siopa. (I went to the shop.)
explanation: Chuig can mean “to” or “towards” and introduces a destination.

question: How do you say “I am tired”?
explanation: Tá tuirse orm is a common expression meaning “I am tired”, literally “tiredness is on me”.

question: Complete: ___ sé anseo anois. (He is here now.)
explanation: Tá is the present form of bí. Bhí is past tense, and beidh is future tense.

question: How do you say “She speaks Irish”?
explanation: The usual word order is verb + subject + object: Labhraíonn sí Gaeilge.

question: Complete: Tá siad ag ___ peile. (They are playing football.)
explanation: After ag in this progressive construction, use the verbal noun: ag imirt.

question: How do you say “We went home”?
explanation: Chuaigh is the past-tense form of téigh, meaning “to go”. Abhaile means “home” when describing movement towards home.

question: Complete: D’ith mé ___. (I ate the apple.)
explanation: An t-úll means “the apple”. The t- is used before a vowel after the singular definite article.

question: How do you say “I don’t understand”?
explanation: Ní thuigim means “I don't understand”. The verb form is lenited after ní.

question: Which means “I am going home now”?
options: Tá mé ag dul abhaile anois.
explanation: Ag dul abhaile means “going home”. Sa bhaile means “at home”, while inné means “yesterday”.

question: How do you ask “Where are you?”
explanation: Cá bhfuil tú? asks about someone's location. Cad means “what” and cé means “who”.

question: Complete: ___ is ainm duit? (What is your name?)
explanation: Cad is ainm duit? is a common way to ask someone's name.

question: Which is a common response to “Go raibh maith agat”?
explanation: Fáilte romhat is a common response meaning “you're welcome”.

question: Complete: Tá cupán tae ___ an mbord. (There is a cup of tea on the table.)
explanation: Ar an mbord means “on the table”. The form of the noun changes after the preposition and article.

question: How do you say “I like music”?
explanation: Is maith liom expresses liking. Literally, it means something like “music is good with me”.

question: Complete: Ní maith ___ caife. (I don't like coffee.)
explanation: Ní maith liom means “I don't like”. Liom is part of this expression.

question: Choose the sentence meaning “The children are playing.”
explanation: The progressive construction uses tá + subject + ag + verbal noun.

question: Complete: Bhí mé ___ an bhaile inné. (I was at home yesterday.)
explanation: Sa bhaile means “at home”. Bhí is the past form of bí, and inné means “yesterday”.

question: How do you say “I saw the woman”?
explanation: Chonaic mé means “I saw”. Chonaic an bhean mé would mean “The woman saw me”.

question: Complete: Tá dhá ___ agam. (I have two cats.)
explanation: The noun after dhá is commonly lenited: dhá chat, “two cats”.

question: Which means “the books”?
explanation: Leabhair is the plural of leabhar, and na is used with plural definite nouns.

question: Complete: Tá mé níos ___ inniu. (I am better today.)
explanation: Níos fearr means “better”. Fearr is the comparative form of maith.

question: How do you say “She is older than me”?
options: Tá sí níos sine ná mé.
explanation: Níos sine ná means “older than”. Ná introduces the comparison.

question: Complete: Tá am ___ agam. (You have time.)
explanation: Agat means “at you” and is used in expressions of possession: tá am agat, “you have time”.

question: How do you say “I can speak a little Irish”?
options: Is féidir liom beagán Gaeilge a labhairt.
Is féidir mé labhairt Gaeilge beagán.
explanation: Is féidir liom is a common construction meaning “I can” or “it is possible for me”.

question: Complete: Ba mhaith liom ___ a ithe. (I'd like to eat something.)
explanation: Rud éigin means “something”; duine éigin means “someone”, and áit éigin means “somewhere”.

question: How do you say “I have no money”?
explanation: Níl aon airgead agam means “I have no money”. Irish expresses possession with agam.

question: Complete: Tá an leabhar ___ spéisiúil. (The book is very interesting.)
explanation: An- intensifies an adjective: an-spéisiúil means “very interesting”.

question: How do you say “I will go tomorrow”?
explanation: Rachaidh is the future form of téigh, “to go”. Amárach means “tomorrow”.

question: Complete: Nuair a ___ mé óg, bhí mé i mo chónaí sa Ghaeltacht. (When I was young...)
explanation: Bhí is the past form of bí. Nuair a bhí mé óg means “when I was young”.

question: Choose the word meaning “because”.
explanation: Mar means “because”; ach means “but”, and nó means “or”.

question: Complete: Tá sé ag obair ___ a dheartháir. (He is working with his brother.)
explanation: Le means “with”. Lena dheartháir means “with his brother”.

question: How do you say “I gave her the book”?
explanation: Thug mé an leabhar di means “I gave her the book”. Di means “to her”.

question: Complete: Is as ___ mé. (I am from Ireland.)
explanation: Is as Éirinn mé is the standard expression for “I am from Ireland”.

question: How do you ask “What are you doing?”
explanation: Cad atá tú a dhéanamh? asks what someone is doing.

question: Which word means “here”?
explanation: Anseo means “here”; inné means “yesterday”, and amárach means “tomorrow”.

question: Which sentence expresses living somewhere for two years, continuing until now?
options: Tá mé i mo chónaí anseo le dhá bhliain.
Bhí mé i mo chónaí anseo dhá bhliain ó shin.
Tá mé i mo chónaí anseo amárach.
explanation: Le dhá bhliain can describe a situation that has continued for two years. Ó shin means “ago”.

question: Complete: Ní raibh ___ agam. (I had no choice.)
explanation: Ní raibh aon rogha agam means “I had no choice”. Aon rogha means “any choice”.

question: Which expression means “although”?
explanation: Cé go means “although”; mar means “because”, and má means “if”.

question: Complete: Tá sí níos airde ___ a deirfiúr. (She is taller than her sister.)
explanation: Ná introduces a comparison: níos airde ná means “taller than”.

question: How do you say “I would like a cup of tea”?
options: Is maith liom cupán tae anois.
explanation: Ba mhaith liom expresses “I would like”.

question: Complete: Dá mbeadh níos mó ama agam, ___ níos mó leabhar. (If I had more time, I would read more books.)
explanation: Léifinn means “I would read”. Dá mbeadh introduces a hypothetical condition.

question: Which expression means “I used to play football”?
options: Ba ghnách liom peil a imirt.
explanation: Ba ghnách liom + verbal noun expresses a habitual past action: “I used to…”.

question: Complete: Tá súil ___ go mbeidh tú ann. (I hope you'll be there.)
explanation: Tá súil agam means “I hope”.

question: Complete: ___ tá am agat, cuir glaoch orm. (If you have time, call me.)
explanation: Má means “if”; nuair means “when”, and cé go means “although”.

question: Complete: Ní hamháin go bhfuil sí cliste, ___ tá sí cineálta freisin. (Not only is she clever, but she is also kind.)
explanation: Ní hamháin ... ach ... freisin means “not only ... but also”.
